s1.syndrome_frame: Multi-system inflammatory syndrome with fever, rash, abdominal symptoms, and cardiovascular involvement
salient_findings: Macular rash on chest and arms
Rising serum creatinine and acute kidney injury
key_facts: 18-year-old African male with no prior medical history
Presented with 2-day history of tonsillitis
Developed abdominal cramping and diarrhea 3 days later
Fever and joint pains in wrists, elbows, and knees
Initial treatment included oral chlorhexidine, lozenges, and symptomatic treatment
Received ceftriaxone, paracetamol, loperamide, and IV methylprednisolone
Deteriorated and transferred to hospital
Febrile, hypotensive, tachycardic, and hypoxemic on arrival
Biliterally coarse crepitations on lung exam
Audible S3 gallop on cardiovascular exam
Abdomen distended and tense with hypoactive bowel sounds
WBC 27.1×10^9/L, Hb 10.9 g/dL, platelets 281×10^9/L
Procalcitonin 71.6 ng/mL, CRP 287 mg/L
Creatinine 494 μmol/L, urea 26.7 mmol/L
Liver tests showed AST 1461 U/L and ALT 812 U/L
Urine albumin:creatinine ratio was 52.3 mg/mmol
Cardiac markers were elevated (troponin 17 137 ng/mL; CK > 7800 U/L)
Chest X-ray showed pulmonary edema and cardiomegaly
Echocardiogram revealed dilated cardiomyopathy with EF 30–35%
Abdominal CT demonstrated distended bowel with splenic and renal infarcts

shortlist.label: Kawasaki disease
shortlist.why_kept: Multi-system inflammatory syndrome with fever, rash, and cardiovascular involvement

shortlist.label: Meningococcemia
shortlist.why_kept: Fever, rash, and multi-organ involvement with elevated inflammatory markers

shortlist.label: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic inflammation, fever, and multi-organ dysfunction

shortlist.label: Rickettsial disease
shortlist.why_kept: Fever, rash, and multi-organ involvement with potential for cardiovascular and abdominal symptoms

shortlist.label: Brucellosis
shortlist.why_kept: Fever, joint pains, and multi-organ involvement with potential for abdominal and cardiovascular symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's rapid deterioration, high fever, rash, abdominal cramping, diarrhea, and laboratory findings such as elevated WBC, procalcitonin, and CRP, along with the presence of splenic and renal infarcts, are consistent with meningococcemia, a severe infection caused by Neisseria meningitidis.

rejected.label: Kawasaki disease
rejected.why: Although Kawasaki disease can present with fever, rash, and abdominal symptoms, the patient's rapid progression to shock, renal infarcts, and elevated cardiac markers are not typical of Kawasaki disease.

rejected.label: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
rejected.why: While hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis can cause fever, abdominal symptoms, and elevated liver enzymes, the patient's presentation with a distinct rash, abdominal cramping, and diarrhea, along with the absence of reported lymphadenopathy or splenomegaly, makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Rickettsial disease
rejected.why: Rickettsial diseases can cause fever, rash, and abdominal symptoms, but the patient's severe presentation with shock, renal infarcts, and elevated cardiac markers, as well as the lack of a reported tick bite or exposure history, makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Brucellosis
rejected.why: Brucellosis can cause fever, abdominal symptoms, and elevated liver enzymes, but the patient's rapid progression to shock, renal infarcts, and elevated cardiac markers, along with the absence of a reported animal exposure history, makes this diagnosis less likely.
